title: Choose the visual world for Ledger
question: A wide, website-style app with a sidebar and separate screens. The roll picked a Platform Board world. Keep it, choose an alternative, or re-roll.

options.label: Platform Board
options.lineage: Indian Railways yellow station boards + Delhi Metro line colours
options.thesis: Your money's journey: totals on a station board, categories as metro lines, transactions set like a timetable.
options.viewport: Black sidebar rail with yellow active line; a yellow station board carrying the bilingual total; trend chart and category route map side by side; the timetable of recent entries below; Add button pinned to the rail.
options.risk: Too much yellow turns it into a costume; the yellow must stay on the one board and the active state.

raised.raise: Colour fills flat and whole: no gradients, glows or grain anywhere on the page.
Every rule is a true 1px hairline on one grid; corners stay square.
All money is tabular numerals in one face, right-aligned to one edge.
Amounts sit right-aligned tight against the column edge, like running times.
Each screen answers one question and fits the viewport without page scroll.

options.label: Rupee Note Series
options.thesis: Each category wears a denomination's colour; totals are set with the fine-line precision of security print.
options.viewport: Light sidebar; a large total framed by a fine-line rosette border; category tiles in note colours; standard table below.
options.risk: The most familiar 'Indian money' idea, and the rosette ornament can slide into decoration.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Everything on one screen: dozens of small ruled modules, each with a red tab header.
options.viewport: Left category rail; a tiled mosaic of KPI, chart, breakdown and recent-entry modules filling 1440×900 with no scroll.
options.case: Holds product clarity (all the analytics in one view) but evaluators and you will not recognise it as yours.
options.risk: Small type is hard to read on a classroom projector.

options.label: Guide Map Lobes
options.thesis: Categories as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.case: Loses both axes: it fights the task, and nothing in it belongs to Indian daily spending.
options.kept: Flat, whole colour fields with no gradients.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One expense fills the screen at a time.
options.viewport: One item per viewport, snap to next.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is portrait by nature, the opposite of what you asked for.
options.kept: One question per screen, fitted to the viewport.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: Two text columns around a vermilion key rail.
options.viewport: Small text block held in a wide margin.
options.case: Loses both axes: a reading form for a working dashboard.
options.risk: Reads as a book, not a tool.
options.kept: One-pixel ruling discipline and square corners.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Side A / Side B tracklists in ballpoint.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to spending, handwriting hurts number legibility.
options.kept: Values right-aligned tight against the edge.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Spending as barcode fields and sine lattices.
options.case: Loses both axes: art installation, not an expense tool.
options.kept: Strict tabular numerals in a single face.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS finance dashboard, like Mint or Monarch, done really well.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, KPI cards across the top, chart grid, table.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other finance dashboard.
